newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Volcano erupts in Russian Far East.
newsitem.headline: Volcano erupts in Russian Far East.

text.p: A volcano erupted in Russia's Far East on Sunday after lying dormant for more than 70 years but there were no reports of damage or injury, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Border guards some 60 km (40 miles) from the 3,528 metre (11,474 feet) Kranotsky peak on the Kamchatka peninsula saw a glow above the volcano, which last erupted in 1923, Tass quoted the Far Eastern centre of the Emergencies Ministry as saying.
It described the eruption as "quiet", unlike other explosive eruptions of Kamchatka's 29 active volcanoes.
The Karymsky volcano erupted in January this year after a powerful earthquake and Russian news agencies said it blasted hot ash about seven km (four miles) into the air.
The Klyuchevskaya Sopka volcano spewed ash 20,000 metres (65,000 feet) into the atmosphere in 1994.
